video_title: Why Bitcoin Wins No Matter What The Fed Does
gist: Despite the title, this is a conversation between Anthony Pompliano and Jordi Visser (ex-hedge fund CIO) arguing that macro obsessives (rates, oil, Fed hikes) are missing the real story: AI progress (Astra) and crypto/tokenization are compounding so fast that the S&P 500 is badly mispriced relative to the actual pace of technological change, and Bitcoin/crypto is entering a mega bull market that could accelerate sharply if the Senate's Clarity Act passes.

themes.theme: Static vs. dynamic thinking and macro obsession

insights.claim: Visser frames a 'static vs dynamic' bucket for market participants: static thinkers extrapolate one data point linearly (tariffs raise prices, therefore inflation), while dynamic thinkers consider second-order responses (domestic manufacturing shifts, policy offsets), and he attributes most 'doomer' macro fear to static thinkers newly arrived online rather than people steeped in AI/crypto's pace of change.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Useful lens for filtering macro commentary: treat single-variable, linear-extrapolation takes (rates+oil=recession) with skepticism versus views that account for policy and behavioral offsets.

insights.claim: Visser argues the current US economy is no longer interest-rate sensitive because growth is driven by AI capex and digital profit margins rather than autos/housing, so debates over a 25bp Fed hike are largely irrelevant to earnings that are growing over 30%.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: If correct, rate-driven bearish macro calls on equities should be discounted; the AI capex/earnings trade is the dominant driver, not the Fed funds rate.
insights.quote: Why anyone would care about this when earnings are growing 30 plus%... there is no rate sensitivity to the AI trade. Zero.

insights.claim: Visser says market structure has three actor classes with different time horizons: leveraged hedge funds with tight drawdown limits that react emotionally to short-term data (like PPI prints), AI trading agents with no emotional drawdown limits that front-run the hedge funds, and long-horizon retail/crypto investors who can buy the dislocations the first two groups create.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Retail/crypto-native investors with a longer horizon can arbitrage the herky-jerky moves created when agents front-run hedge funds reacting to stale macro data points.

themes.theme: Crypto valuation, tokenization and the Clarity Act

insights.claim: Visser is writing a research paper arguing crypto (specifically Ethereum) should be valued as an 'ecosystem' the way the early internet was, since traditional metrics (eyeballs, clicks in the 1990s) proved meaningless and crypto currently lacks agreed valuation metrics.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Investors should be wary of dismissing crypto valuations as 'unjustifiable' using traditional metrics the same way 1990s skeptics dismissed Amazon before eyeball/ecosystem value later validated it.

insights.claim: Robinhood is being re-rated by Wall Street (Morgan Stanley upgrade) not for crypto revenue but because it is becoming an Apple-like multi-revenue-stream business spanning traditional stock trading, Robinhood Chain (crypto/tokenization via Arbitrum), and agentic/AI trading tools, and now reportedly earns more from prediction markets than stock trading commissions.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Robinhood is presented as the single best public proxy for the 'AI-crypto-macro nexus' merge thesis; worth tracking as a barometer stock for tokenization adoption.

insights.claim: Visser believes passage of the Clarity Act (crypto market structure legislation) would be a major bullish catalyst because it would let pension funds -- which need regulatory cover to satisfy fiduciary duty -- begin allocating to the crypto ecosystem, a bigger incremental buyer pool than venture capital.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Clarity Act passage is a catalyst to watch; prediction markets were pricing it below 20% for this year as of the taping, so any positive surprise could be a mispriced upside trigger for crypto.
insights.quote: if clarity goes through, I think the ecosystem will be valued higher immediately because I think this opens up investment from pension funds

insights.claim: Ethereum was the best-performing major asset (>$100B market cap) quarter-to-date as of the taping, roughly doubling Bitcoin's return while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq were roughly flat, which Visser reads as low correlation that could pull equities up alongside crypto in the next leg.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: A quarter of crypto outperformance with flat equities is framed as evidence of decoupling that could presage equities catching up rather than crypto reverting.

themes.theme: AI progress outrunning the market's macro obsession

insights.claim: Visser says OpenAI's Astra represents a step-function jump beyond Grok that combines agentic capability, chat, work and image generation, and that AI progress is now compounding day-to-day rather than week-to-week.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Signals accelerating capability releases as a reason equity terminal values for AI-exposed companies may need continual upward revision.

insights.claim: Visser cites an OpenAI model reportedly solving progress on a Navier-Stokes-related century-old math problem using ~100,000 GPUs of brute-force compute, and argues this level of physics/math breakthrough threatens the terminal value of traditional physical/mining companies 5+ years out, even though it won't affect near-term (3-4 year) earnings.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Long-duration investors in commodity/mining/physical-science-dependent industries should consider terminal-value risk from AI-driven scientific breakthroughs, not just near-term earnings.

insights.claim: Visser argues the S&P 500 has been roughly flat since around June 2nd despite what he considers landmark AI progress (Astra, AGI claims, math/physics breakthroughs), meaning the market is badly mispriced relative to the pace of innovation and is primed to move sharply higher once it 'catches up.'
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: A bull thesis for US equities predicated on a re-rating catch-up trade once macro fear (midterms, Fed, oil) fades and investors refocus on AI fundamentals.
insights.quote: The market's completely mispriced relative to the progress that's happening.

insights.claim: Visser notes Jensen Huang publicly congratulated OpenAI on reaching AGI in the same week Treasury Secretary Bessent was fielding questions about Fed rate hikes and oil, illustrating the disconnect between headline AI milestones and what mainstream market commentary is focused on.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: A concrete illustration of the 'market missing the AI story' thesis worth citing when arguing that macro chatter is crowding out more important AI-driven fundamentals.

insights.claim: Visser argues H100 GPU compute prices have risen year-over-year rather than depreciating (per Gavin Baker's analysis), undercutting the Michael Burry/Jim Chanos bear thesis that AI chips depreciate too fast to justify capex, and implying cloud providers' profits could inflect faster than expected from both new data centers and higher pricing on existing GPUs with falling relative costs.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Direct rebuttal to the 'AI bubble/depreciation' bear case; if compute pricing power is rising, cloud/hyperscaler margins may surprise to the upside sooner than bears expect.

insights.claim: Visser cites reports that Iran fed war plans, targeting lists and other sensitive material into Claude, and that Anthropic identified and blocked the misuse, framing this alongside a UK power-plant hack and a Boston Scientific hacking incident (which forced the company to cut earnings guidance) as evidence that AI-enabled cyberattacks on critical infrastructure are now a live, underappreciated risk.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Raises critical-infrastructure cybersecurity (referencing his portfolio company Galvanick) as an investable theme given AI-enabled attack capability is outpacing defense at less-sophisticated organizations (utilities, hospitals) versus well-resourced tech firms.

insights.claim: Visser draws a parallel between the Iran/Claude misuse story and allegations that OpenAI may have trained on questions related to unsolved math problems before appearing to solve them, arguing both episodes show that data security and 'owning your own intelligence' are becoming critical strategic concerns.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Frames data security/model-training provenance as an emerging governance and competitive-moat issue for enterprises and AI labs alike.

insights.claim: Visser believes a Fed hike (with a dovish 'insurance' framing) is actually more market-friendly than no hike at all, because a dovish hike preserves Fed credibility while a decision not to hike could raise questions about political independence and leave the door open to future hikes.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: A scenario-based framework for how markets might react to the upcoming FOMC decision: hike+dovish message > no hike > hike+hawkish message (least likely).

insights.claim: Visser argues 10-year Treasury yields have structurally traded below nominal GDP since 1997 (versus ~200bps above nominal GDP historically), and that this gap persists because the economy is no longer rate-sensitive (autos/housing), making current 10-year yields insufficiently restrictive by his framework even as doomers call for higher rates to fight inflation.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: A structural argument for why yields near current levels aren't restrictive enough to matter for AI-driven growth, relevant to debates about whether high rates will choke the AI trade.

insights.claim: Visser argues the administration (Trump, Bessent, and Fed nominee Kevin Warsh, who is described as pro-crypto and pro-Bitcoin and influenced by Alan Greenspan's view that transformative technology should change Fed policy) is aligned in supporting AI and crypto, making it risky to bet against either asset class given the White House's stated position that the US 'cannot lose the AI race to China.'
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Political alignment behind AI/crypto is framed as a tailwind investors should respect rather than fight, given policymakers are actively working with AI labs.
